about: The five span types J2 asks for (DIRECTOR-PLAN-W2.md §3 J2), with the descriptions a label may carry into the prompt, and the rules the fixtures were labelled by. Descriptions deliberately name no word that appears in a fixture.

types.name: measurement name
types.description: the name of a body or garment measurement, such as hip, inseam or neck

types.name: quantity
types.description: a number, a count or a range of numbers, as written

types.name: unit
types.description: a unit of length or angle, or its symbol, such as cm, feet or degrees

types.name: garment or part name
types.description: a garment, or a named part of the thing being made, such as a sleeve, a roof or a node

types.name: operation
types.description: an arithmetic operation or a verb for one, such as plus, minus, times, divided by or halve

rules: Label the words as the drafter wrote them, by what they are, and nothing the text does not say.
measurement name: the whole name of a measured dimension, connecting words included (Top shoulder to under armpit), and an allowance (seam allowance).
quantity: a number or a number word, as written; a range is ONE span (3–6, 72–74, 0.8…3.0) and a sign written on the number belongs to it (+29, -1.8…1.0).
unit: a unit word or symbol that goes with a quantity (", inch, inches, u, °, world units).
garment or part name: a garment (apron dress), or a named part of the thing being made (towers, wall, gate, a decision, tops, part 1).

operation: an arithmetic operator (+ − × ÷ /) or a verb that performs one (Add), and in the shard's brief the ops a reply may ask of a part (raise, cut, mirror, take it out). An = is not an operation: in a running total it marks the next value.

ignore: spans a careful annotator could type either way, or that belong to another seat, are listed with their reason. A prediction inside one is neither credited nor counted wrong; an ignored span is never required. Step numbers are the decision seat's (J1: is this number an amount or a step?); letter keys and references (A, B, C, ①) are the sheet's (M2); the whole thing being made is neither a garment nor a part (castle, flowchart); ids and the shard brief's words for its own machinery are not words the human wrote.
